Classification and constraints\n12\t- **What:** one line on the system.\n13\t- **Type:** software / infra / AI-agentic (or a mix); greenfield or brownfield; small build or not.\n14\t- **Dominant constraint:** correctness | availability | latency | cost | scale | compliance.\n15\t- **Worst failure:** the single failure that would hurt most.\n16\t\n17\t**Budgets** (only the rows that bind; add rows the system needs, such as a cutover freeze window):\n18\t\n19\t| Budget | Target | Label | Checked by |\n20\t|---|---|---|---|\n21\t| Latency | … | REQUIREMENT / BASELINE / ASSUMPTION / UNKNOWN | V… or Phase … |\n22\t| Throughput | … | … | … |\n23\t| Availability / SLO | … | … | … |\n24\t| RPO / RTO | … | … | … |\n25\t| Resource use | … | … | … |\n26\t| AI inference cost | … (AI systems only) | … | … |\n27\t| Storage cost | … | … | … |\n28\t| Operational complexity | … (e.g. services to run, on-call load) | … | … |\n29\t\n30\tAn UNKNOWN target has no number: write the missing input, who supplies it, and the phase that\n31\tneeds it. An ASSUMPTION gives its basis.\n32\t\n33\t**Missing inputs:** the unknowns that would change the plan most, and any assumption the phase\n34\torder rests on.\n35\t\n36\t## 2. Dependency map\n37\tOnly the dependencies that bind and that the phase order does not already show:\n38\t\n39\t| What waits | Depends on | Kind | Blocked from being |\n40\t|---|---|---|---|\n41\t| … | … | decision / validation / risk-security / organizational / economic (structural or runtime only when surprising) | built / deployed / specified / hardened / exposed / committed |\n42\t\n43\tThen one line naming the kinds with no instance (\"No organizational or economic dependencies.\").\n44\tIn brownfield work, mark each dependency CONFIRMED or ASSUMED.\n45\t\n46\t## 3. Tradeoff gates (resolved up front)\n47\t\n48\t| Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition |\n49\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n50\t| Consistency vs availability | R2/R3 + one-clause reason | … | … | V…, a cheap check, or the cited basis | … (for a gated row: \"V… fails, or …\") |\n51\t| Monolith vs services | … | … | … | … | … |\n52\t| Sync vs async | … | … | … | … | … |\n53\t| Build vs buy | … | … | … | … | … |\n54\t| Data-privacy boundary (personal or regulated data) | … | … | … | … | … |\n55\t| <each system-specific R2/R3 decision, e.g. the tenancy model> | … | … | … | … | … |\n56\t| (Brownfield) migration strategy, coexistence and cutover, rollback, system of record | … | … | … | … | … |\n57\t| (AI) prompt+RAG vs fine-tune | … | … | … | … | … |\n58\t| (AI) hosted API vs self-host | … | … | … | … | … |\n59\t\n60\t**R1 defaults:** <decision> → <default>; … (one line; no rows for R1 decisions).\n61\t**N/A:** <considered decisions that do not apply> — <reason> (one line).\n62\tOmit the (Brownfield) and (AI) rows when they do not apply. It shows the plan before applying it, and every applied run can be undone.\n- **Type:** Software only, with no AI component. Greenfield. Small build: one developer, no outside service, no money, no regulated data. The photos are personal data, though, because EXIF holds GPS position and timestamps.\n- **Dominant constraint:** Correctness. No photo may be lost, overwritten or given the wrong date.\n- **Worst failure:** A filename collision makes one photo silently overwrite another. On POSIX, `os.rename` replaces an existing target, so this can happen. The photo is gone for good. The case-insensitive filesystems used on Windows and macOS make collisions more likely, and so do burst shots taken in the same second.\n\n**Budgets**\n\n| Budget | Target | Label | Checked by |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Data safety | 0 files lost or overwritten. Baseline measured at V0 | Phase 2 exit |\n| Resource use | ≤ 200 MB RSS for a 50k-file folder | ASSUMPTION (each plan entry is under 1 KB) | Phase 2 exit |\n| Operational complexity | No services. Tradeoff gates\n\n| Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Plan unit and journal contract | R2: planner, journal and undo all build on it, and changing it breaks old journals | The unit is a **file group** sharing one stem: photo, `.xmp`, `.aae`, RAW+JPEG pair, Live Photo `.MOV`. The journal is JSONL with `schema_version` and, per group, the original path, new path and SHA-256 | Real folders contain sidecars that must stay paired | Cheap check, Phase 1: the corpus includes each sidecar type and every group pairs correctly | Real files share a stem but are different shots: switch to a per-file unit with explicit sidecar matching |\n| Collision policy and rename primitive | R3: one overwrite destroys a photo for good, even if it's noticed seconds later | Never overwrite. Collisions get deterministic `_1`, `_2` suffixes, ordered by `SubSecTimeOriginal` and then by original name. Renames use each OS's no-replace call: `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` on Linux, `renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL)` on macOS, `MoveFileExW` without `REPLACE_EXISTING` on Windows. Collisions are compared case-folded | These calls hold on ext4, APFS, NTFS and exFAT | V2 | V2 fails on any filesystem: use copy mode there (write renamed copies to a new folder and leave originals untouched) |\n| Privacy boundary (EXIF GPS, file paths) | R3: leaked location data can't be recalled | Fully offline: no network code, no telemetry, no update check. The rename step runs **dry-run only**, printing \"would rename\". Nothing gets renamed until V2 passes.\n- **Deployed:** GitHub Actions builds the wheel from a tag and publishes a pre-release to TestPyPI with trusted publishing. Classification and constraints\n- **What:** A local command-line tool. Small build: one developer, no outside service, no money, no regulated data. The photos are personal data, though, because EXIF holds GPS position and timestamps.\n- **Dominant constraint:** Correctness. No photo may be lost, overwritten or given the wrong date.\n- **Worst failure:** A filename collision makes one photo silently overwrite another. On POSIX, `os.rename` replaces an existing target, so this can happen. The photo is gone for good.
